description:
A Roman period church associated with a cemetery outside the south-eastern walls of the Roman city of Camulodunum. Based on the evidence of pottery and coinage the church appears to have been constructed around the early 3rd CE and have fallen into disuse by the late 4th or early 4th CE, though its ruins still stood even into modern times. 

The church is particularly unique because of four pits around the apse of the church which produced a wide array of finds including coins, animal bones, jewellery, utensils, and a human skull and thigh bone. This assemblage, especially coming out of pits is much more in line with what we might expect from a temple or shrine, and in those contexts they may have been interpreted as votive deposits.

A square building is just outside of the church and dates from the same period, it appears to be simple and utilitarian with a central heart. It may have been a space for preparing food for funerary feasting. A possible mausoleum was also found in the same cemetery.
